name: Six Bells

The rear garden offers sunny spots and a pergola draped in greenery in summer—ideal for relaxed get-togethers. There’s also a large function room with an exclusive bar for celebrations, events and even movies, with the restaurant available for exclusive hire.

name: Earl of Beaconsfield

There’s a beer garden for warmer days, plus bookings and baby changing facilities. Sports fans can enjoy TNT Sports and Sky Sports, and the venue runs regular activities including weekly quizzes and live music, alongside seasonal events.

name: The Empress

name: White Swan
description: A late-night favourite in a bohemian pocket of Cambridge, known for its friendly mix of locals, visitors and students. name: Baron of Beef
description: Step into a traditional, Grade II listed Cambridge pub with old-world charm and a warm, welcoming feel. It’s a great spot for food and drinks, with a menu covering pub classics, small plates and a proper Sunday roast. There’s a beer garden for weather-permitting drinks, plus WiFi and takeaway. If you’re coming for sport, expect a proper match-day atmosphere with Sky Sports and TNT Sports, and fixtures for football, tennis and cricket. Dogs and families are catered for, and you can book ahead for a relaxed visit.

name: The Mitre
description: Step into a traditional Cambridge pub with a distinctive character, just a short stroll from Trinity Street, Sidney Street and Round Church Street. Expect a classic British menu built around quality pub food and “famous British hospitality”, plus an eclectic range of real ales. There’s plenty of ways to dine too—book a table, order at the table, or choose collection—making it easy to drop in for a proper pint and a pie-style meal.

name: Champion of the Thames
description: A pocket-sized King Street institution with wood-panelled Victorian rooms, etched rowing windows and a buzz of student and local regulars. Named for a Thames sculling champion who insisted his mail be sent to King Street, it remains on the notorious King Street Run and hosts an annual cricket match against St Radegund. CAMRA Cambridgeshire Pub of the Year 2024, the Champ pours immaculate Greene King and guest ales alongside pork pies, scotch eggs and Sunday cheese and crackers in a nationally listed historic interior.

name: Prince Regent
description: Set in the heart of Cambridge, this traditional pub-restaurant blends history with a lively, family-friendly welcome. Expect cask ales, classic pub favourites and a menu with small plates and hearty options, plus Sunday roasts. There’s a beer garden for weather-permitting drinks, and WiFi and takeaway are available. Sports fans can settle in for live football across major leagues and competitions, with TNT Sports and Sky Sports mentioned. Dogs are explicitly welcomed, making it a comfortable local for groups and casual meet-ups.

name: The Castle Bar
description: A city-centre stop with a laid-back bar downstairs and six guest rooms upstairs, ideal for a competitive stay in Cambridge. Set in a building of special interest, it’s a handy base for meeting friends, enjoying a drink and exploring on foot. Expect on-site entertainment with music in the bar on Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays late into the night. Facilities include free WiFi, baggage storage and bike lock-up, plus family-friendly touches like highchairs. If you need support during your stay, the team asks you to flag it when booking.

name: d'Arry's
description: Set on King Street in the centre of Cambridge, this independent restaurant, bar and cheesemonger brings together seasonal dining, barrel-aged cocktails and a serious cheese programme. Expect locally sourced meat, sustainable seafood and fresh vegetables, plus a celebrated Sunday Carvery. Upstairs, The Liquor Loft is a stylish wine and cocktail hideaway that’s available for private hire. For foodies, there are cheese tasting experiences led by Academy of Cheese-trained experts. There’s also an apartment above the venue for a stay-in-Cambridge break, ideal for turning a great meal into a proper night out.

name: The Waterman
description: A modern Cambridge inn with a welcoming, all-day feel—just a short stroll from Midsummer Common and near the River Cam. Settle into cosy interiors or head out to the courtyard/garden terrace, with heat lamps for cooler evenings. The bar focuses on craft beer, an eclectic wine and spirits range, and spritzes, while the kitchen serves fresh, flavour-driven seasonal dishes, pub classics and indulgent burgers. There’s also a “Potting Shed” event space for parties and meetings, plus comfortable rooms above the pub for leisurely stays. Expect match-day energy too, with big screens and proper sound for major tournaments.

name: The Punter
description: A cheerfully scrappy, lived-in pub in Cambridge’s Quayside area, set in an old coaching inn with quirky nooks and low ceilings (the Barn has a high vaulted space). Expect a homely, welcoming atmosphere with a courtyard packed with planting—ideal for a summer afternoon. The kitchen serves freshly made, unpretentious but hearty food, with set food service windows across the week. With its central-but-riverside location, it’s a handy stop for walkers heading towards the museums and nearby attractions.

name: Carpenters Arms
description: A craft beer pub in the heart of Cambridge, built for sports fans and pizza lovers. Expect stone-baked pizza, craft beer and regular deals like Monday 2-4-1 pizzas, plus a weekly quiz night. There’s live sport showing (including World Cup coverage) and a lively, social atmosphere in the bar area. Dogs are welcome to join you there, and the venue also highlights free Wi‑Fi and a beer garden for when the weather’s good. Kitchen hours are listed, though the kitchen is temporarily closed for maintenance.

name: Green Dragon
description: A characterful, historic pub in the heart of Chesterton, set with stunning riverside views. Expect a picturesque beer garden that leads down towards the river, plus a solid selection of cask ales and wines. Food is a highlight too, with home-cooked fresh dishes and a Lebanese street food kitchen with set opening times. If you’re into the river action, it’s also noted as a great place to catch the rowing activity during the May Bumps and Town bumps in June. Quizzes run fortnightly, making it a friendly local for relaxed evenings by the water.

name: Panton Arms
description: Set in central Cambridge, this traditional British pub is known for a welcoming, chatty atmosphere and a standout bar. Expect quality cask ales, rotating guest beers, plus wines, premium gins and plenty of bottled options including gluten-free and alcohol-free. Dogs are welcome both inside and in the courtyard garden, with water and treats provided. There’s plenty going on too: a weekly Irish Folk Jam (Thursday evenings) and monthly live music, alongside two large-screen TVs showing terrestrial sports such as rugby and international football. Book ahead for drinks when it gets busy.

name: The Alma
description: A friendly Cambridge rugby-and-real-ale pub with a warm, welcoming atmosphere. Settle in for Sky Sports, TNT Sport and Premier Sports on three big screens, then make a night of it with weekly quiz prizes and a free singer-songwriter open mic (Songsmith Sessions) on the third Sunday. Tuesdays bring Curry Night with a choice of seven curries when bought with a drink. The kitchen serves traditional homecooked pub food for lunches, snacks and evening meals, plus six well-kept real ales and a Cask Marque accreditation.

name: Green Man
description: Set on Trumpington High Street, this Grade II listed medieval timber frame hides behind later brickwork yet still feels like a proper country pub on the edge of Cambridge. Mitchells & Butlers runs a food-led house with an open-plan bar, high-roofed restaurant and a garden seating around two hundred. Adnams Broadside and Sharp's Doom Bar anchor the taps while extensive menus run from weekend breakfasts to Sunday roasts, making it as much a dining destination as a pint stop after a riverside walk.

name: Hudson's Ale House
description: Set in the heart of Trumpington, this community pub pairs a classic Cambridge feel with a garden vibe. Expect a strong beer focus with hand pumps and a rotating community calendar, including live music and regular quiz nights. Food is a standout too: the pub’s Tzatziki kitchen brings authentic Greek cuisine to takeaway and pub dining. With easy car parking at the rear and a central High Street address, it’s a friendly local for drinks, events, and laid-back evenings.

name: Blue Ball Inn
description: Grantchester's oldest pub, dating from 1767 and rebuilt after an nineteenth-century fire, retains a cosy two-bar layout on the National Inventory of Historic Pub Interiors. No televisions or fruit machines—conversation, East Anglian real ales from Adnams, Woodforde's and Elgood's, and old pub games such as ring the bull set the tone. A walled garden with covered heated area, piano and cricket memorabilia backs onto meadow views towards the river and colleges. Home-cooked lunches and evening meals, B&B rooms and a dog-friendly welcome make this free house the unofficial headquarters of Grantchester Cricket Club.

The kitchen is open every day, serving a modern British menu with seasonal dishes and local suppliers, from quick bites to celebratory three-course suppers. There’s also garden dining for relaxed outdoor meals. When you fancy staying, there are four cosy bedrooms, and the place is dog-friendly with a special menu for furry guests. Set up for gatherings, birthdays and family meals, with woodland and the village common nearby for walks.

name: The Fountain
description: A Grade II listed, 15th-century pub in Soham with a friendly, easy-going feel. Drop in for cask-marked real ale and a cocktail menu, then settle in for live sport on HD screens—showing major tournaments and every match. There’s a beer garden/outside area for warmer days, plus a dartboard, pool table and function space for groups. With a late licence and live entertainment/live music listed, it’s a lively spot for watching the game and enjoying great drink offers.

name: Comrades Club
description: Set on Market Street in Soham, this well-established club has two bars serving beers, wines and spirits—ideal for a relaxed drink with friends. When the weather’s good, there’s an outdoor beer garden for summer sessions. Inside you can get competitive with a snooker and pool table, adding a social, games-led feel to the evening. Keep an eye on the club’s events page for what’s on.

name: Red Lion
description: A 17th-century inn in Soham with roaring fires for cosy winter evenings and a lovely walled garden for al fresco dining in summer. The kitchen focuses on rustic, modern cooking with local, seasonal ingredients, with lunch and dinner service plus Sunday dining. There’s also a dedicated event space for up to 75 guests, and you can drop in for cocktails—there’s a cocktail hour between 6pm and 7pm. Dogs and children are welcome across the restaurant and garden, making it a relaxed choice for groups and casual get-togethers.

name: The Ship
description: Set on Soham High Street, this friendly open-plan town-centre pub combines an inglenook fire with pool table, dartboard and jukebox. Three televisions show sports and racing channels, quiz nights run on Wednesdays and a pool team competes locally, while live music with bands or DJs features at least monthly on Fridays and Saturdays thanks to a late licence. A partially undercover patio and grassed area at the end of the car park suit summer drinking, and an annual August gin fest and beer festival add to the calendar. Real ale is available alongside a wide gin selection.

name: The Castle Inn
description: Set in the heart of the city, this independent pub serves fine beers, wines and spirits alongside home-cooked favourites. Expect standout dishes like Black-Rock cooked steaks, with kitchen hours running through lunch and evening. There’s plenty of space for gatherings, from a cosy snug in the main bar to the entire upper floor, plus table service via a web app for ordering and pay-at-table. The venue also leans into community with a house charity and regular food promos such as £10 burger Wednesdays. With an extensive garden and easy nearby parking, it’s a welcoming stop for drinks and a proper meal.

name: King Street Run
description: Self-confessedly quirky, this King Street institution commemorates the famous pint-to-pint challenge that once linked eight pubs along the road. Refitted decades ago as a fun pub, it still wears the scars—carpets and furniture fixed to the ceiling—while upstairs proves even more higgledy-piggledy than the bare-boarded U-shaped ground floor with unused fireplaces, table football and television screens. An alternative-leaning, friendly crowd gathers for happy hour on weekday evenings. Upstairs hosts two pool tables, bar billiards and extra seating, with Sky and TNT sports on multiple screens.

name: The Grain & Hop Store
description: A contemporary Cambridge pub built for groups, with craft beer and cocktails plus a proper menu of burgers, pies and fish & chips. Settle in for live football atmosphere with Sky Sports and TNT Sports, and catch the action with fixtures and big tournament seat bookings. There’s a weather-permitting beer garden, WiFi and cashless pool table, dartboard and shuffleboard for laid-back competition. Families and dogs are welcome, and there’s a weekly pub quiz every Thursday. For nights out, try the karaoke pods—book a table and step into the spotlight.

name: The Pint Shop
description: Opened in November 2013 in a handsome Georgian townhouse where E.M. Forster once lived, this was Cambridge's first new pub in over a decade and helped spark a city-centre revival. Three floors of drinking and dining rooms surround a rear terraced patio garden separated from a smokers' alley. Four changing cask ales and two real ciders share bar space with seventeen keg lines emphasising UK and European craft beer, while an extensive gin list and seasonal British menu—from scotch eggs to charcoal-grilled mains—complete the offering. Dogs are welcome in the bar and garden.

name: Station Tavern
description: A quirky, cosy stop-off right by Cambridge train station, with a welcoming bar, an outdoor terrace for sunny afternoons, and a function room for parties and corporate gatherings. Expect a fresh, traditional seasonal British menu with ever-changing mains, plus sides and bar snacks. The bar is fully loaded with craft beers, an extensive wine list and a go-to selection of iconic cocktails, including a seasonal spritz menu with alcohol-free options. If you’re here for sport, settle in for World Cup action on big screens and enjoy a proper matchday atmosphere.

name: Old Ticket Office
description: A beautifully restored pub right by Cambridge Railway Station, made for quick pints, long waits and easy meet-ups. Expect well-kept cask ales, rotating craft beers and a solid range of wines, ciders, spirits and soft drinks. There’s a bottle-shop for takeaways, plus a hatch window on Platform 4 serving Arabica coffee until 7pm and bacon or sausage baps from 7am–12pm. With big screens for major tournaments and a terrace for lingering, it’s a lively stop that still feels relaxed—whether you’re arriving, exploring or catching the next train.

name: The Three Horseshoes
description: Set in the friendly village of Stapleford, this independent pub is known for award-winning hospitality and a proper cask beer focus, with frequent rotations across multiple hand pumps. Expect a seasonal menu alongside a well-chosen drinks list, working with local wine merchants. There’s an enclosed garden and plenty of parking, making it easy for families and visitors with dogs. Kitchen service runs most days with clear midday and evening windows, and you can book for groups—plus they offer group meze bookings.

name: The Bird or Worm?
description: Opened in July 2021 on Newmarket Road, this smart ground-floor bar occupies a building that also houses Ninja Theory, the BAFTA-winning games studio behind Hellblade. The name nods to a poignant moment in an early Ninja Theory game, and the venue replaced the former Five Bells site. Three BrewBoard keg taps pour local craft beer—no cask—but cocktails, wines and spirits accompany a menu from snacks and salads to burgers and eclectic global mains. Stylish decor, a boardroom table near the entrance and weekday-only hours give it a discreet, office-adjacent feel.

name: The Regal - JD Wetherspoon
description: Housed in the art-deco shell of Cambridge's 1937 Regal cinema, this vast Wetherspoon occupies two floors of what was once billed as Britain's biggest pub when it opened in 2000. CAMRA lists it in the Good Beer Guide with four regular ales plus eight to ten rotating guests from brewers such as Adnams, Greene King and Sharp's. A licensed rear patio offers outdoor drinking, while the app-driven food menu keeps lunch and dinner affordable. Friday and Saturday nights bring a DJ from ten o'clock, and TV screens show sport throughout. Expect queues and busy service on weekend evenings in this city-centre landmark.

name: The Petersfield
description: Backstreet Sturton Street gained a serious drinking destination when this former White Hart and acclaimed Backstreet Bistro returned to pub life in February 2017. A large L-shaped bar mixes traditional wood and plush furnishings with five handpumps pouring the likes of Barsham, Nene Valley and Adnams, plus keg craft lines from Cambridge Brewing Company. Trust Inns took over from Young's in April 2026. Food runs from modern gastropub menus to Sunday service, with a terrace splitting smoking and non-smoking areas. A quieter snug behind the bar suits smaller groups. CAMRA members enjoy a ten percent discount at this Petersfield neighbourhood favourite.

name: The Maypole
description: A family-run independent pub in Cambridge city centre, tucked between Bridge Street and Jesus Green. Expect a traditional feel with a continental, Mediterranean twist—served up alongside a big, ever-changing selection of real ales and craft beers. Settle into the lounge bar, then head outside to a large covered, heated beer garden with hand-painted mural artwork. There’s also an upstairs bar for dining and private hire, plus a newly renovated back bar reached via a “secret door”. Food is centred on quality homemade Italian dishes, with pizzas and cocktails mentioned by visitors.

name: Robin Hood
description: A family-friendly Greene King pub in Cherry Hinton, Cambridge, with a warm, welcoming feel and a focus on grilled cuisine. Drop in for pub classics, seasonal spring drinks, and a proper breakfast menu, plus plenty of beer choice. There’s a beer garden for sunny days, and practical extras like WiFi, EV charging, car park and coach acceptance. If you’re bringing the dog, the venue is explicitly dog friendly. Expect regular match-day buzz too, with World Cup booking promotions and a “world’s game” theme.

name: The Alex
description: A lively Cambridge pub with a strong food focus—burgers and mains are available to eat in or take away, plus a rotating draught beer and cider selection. You can order and pay for food and drink to be delivered to your table or collect it. The venue also runs regular events, including Sunday sessions featuring live traditional music. Book ahead for a table, the garden room, or the garden, and keep an eye on seasonal updates and special offers.

name: Dobblers Inn
description: Genuine backstreet character defines this Wells & Co local near the Grafton Centre, where licensees celebrated twenty-one years in July 2023 and CAMRA crowned it City Community Pub of the Year 2019. Formerly Whitbread's City Arms, the pub retains décor from its CAMRA Investments era and pours Cask Marque-accredited Brewpoint ales. Sport is central: Sky and TNT screens, plus teams for football, cricket, darts, pool and cribbage. A courtyard beer garden with heated smoking area is widely praised. Tuesday quiz nights and occasional cider festivals draw a loyal crowd drawn from every walk of Cambridge life.

name: The Geldart
description: A warm, friendly back-street pub in central Cambridge, built around a cosy real-ale bar with an open fire. Expect a great range of cask ales, draught beers, fine wines, whiskies and rums, plus home-cooked pub specials and innovative “hot rock” meals. Lunchtime Sunday roasts are on the menu. There’s also a large restaurant and a beautiful courtyard garden for a relaxed drink in the open air. Regular live music keeps the evenings lively—check the events listing to plan your visit.

name: Monkfield Arms
description: A lively village pub in Cambourne with plenty happening after dark, plus a proper focus on food and drink. Drop in for a quick pint or settle down for a meal from a varied menu, including Sunday roasts. Expect well-kept cask ales alongside world lagers, wines and spirits. There’s a beer garden for dining outdoors, and the venue is dog-friendly in the bar area. For matchday, it leans into World Cup vibes with big screens across bar and dining spaces, plus quizzes and special events like karaoke and tribute nights. Facilities include a pool table, dartboard and car park.

name: The Boot
description: Set in the heart of Histon village, opposite the village green and close to Cambridge, this characterful pub blends a cosy bar and snug with a bright dining space. Expect seasonal, fresh food alongside well-poured pints, a curated wine list and cocktails. There’s an extensive garden with terrace outdoor dining, plus an undercover heated tent for year-round comfort. Dogs are welcome in the bar and garden, and you’ll find family-friendly touches like a kids menu and even a dog menu. With a car park on site and regular “What’s on” events including steak nights, roasts, happy hour and live sessions, it’s a proper local hub.

name: The Red Lion
description: A much-loved village beer house in Histon with a warm, settle-in feel—ideal for relaxed lunches, evenings with friends, or a quiet drink at the bar. Expect seasonal pub classics and a proper menu, plus lighter options and sharing dishes. When the big moments hit, there are big screens and a lively World Cup atmosphere. There’s also a cosy stay: four modern en-suite boutique rooms, along with a Bottle Room for private celebrations. Keep an eye on quizzes and community events, and enjoy summer spritzes in the pub and garden.

name: The Barley Mow
description: Histon's village local reopened under new owners Mishah and Chelsea in April 2025 after turnover followed Dore McCann's retirement and a Greene King Hive spell. The dog-leg single bar now pairs an outside bar and pizza oven with Thai curries, Sunday roasts and Italian-inspired dishes using 72-hour dough. An impressively large rear garden and front seating host live bands and DJ nights through summer. Pool has returned alongside craft cocktails and rentable pétanque on the lawn. Greene King IPA remains a regular cask line amid a refreshed draught selection in this revived CB24 favourite.

name: The Fox
description: A modern, family-friendly pub in Bar Hill, tucked between Lolworth and Dry Drayton. Settle into the lively local atmosphere at Gladeside, with a menu built around proper pub classics, hearty roasts and bar snacks, plus small plates for kids. The bar is stocked with lagers, spirits, wines and cocktails—ideal for everything from a casual pint to game-day celebrations. Expect regular entertainment nights (including live music from 8pm) and plenty of sport coverage, with World Cup and match-day buzz, plus quiz nights and special promotions.

name: Milton Arms
description: Set on the outskirts of Cambridge, this family-friendly Hungry Horse pub-restaurant is built for easy dining and big-match nights. Expect a Hungry Horse menu with classic pub favourites like stacked burgers, plus breakfast and daily deals. When sport’s on, settle in for Sky Sports and TNT Sports with big screens and fixtures across major leagues and internationals. There’s also a cashless pool table and dartboard for laid-back competition, WiFi, EV charging and a car park. In summer, the beer garden adds extra space for kids and grown-ups alike.

name: Red Lion
description: Lavishly thatched and designed by Basil Oliver in 1936, this Grantchester gastropub stands on foundations dating to 1777 when it traded as the Axe & Saw. Metropolitan Pub Company, Greene King's premium wing, runs a polished interior of wainscotting, panelling and mixed flooring around a sturdy wooden bar, with a large restaurant, private dining room and multi-level garden of patio, decking and lawn. Seasonal British menus use local suppliers where possible, with prix fixe lunch offers midweek. Dogs are welcome, and live sport screens for major fixtures. Regional guest ales complement Greene King IPA on the pumps.

name: The Tivoli
description: A four-floor riverside playground in Cambridge, built for groups who want food, drinks and games under one roof. Expect crazy golf, shuffleboard and augmented-reality darts, plus bars on every level. When the mood turns social, there are private hire spaces for birthdays, team socials and big takeovers. Food options include pizza and burgers, with cocktails, wines and great beers to match. Sports fans can catch big-screen action during football tournaments and fixtures, with DJs, quizzes and regular events keeping the energy high. Rooftop spritz sessions and family-friendly game pass Sundays make it easy to plan a visit.

name: Old Spring
description: A lively Cambridge pub on Ferry Path, open daily from midday until late. Expect a proper food-led calendar: Greek Night every Thursday and Friday from 6pm, plus a Sunday roast service running 12–6 with beef, chicken and pork. There are weekly signature dishes and blackboard specials, and roast dinners are limited so booking is advised. The 241 Cocktail Club runs every Thursday 4–8pm with 2-for-1 cocktails. There’s also space for buffet and party bookings, and parking is available with on-site car registration.

name: The Boathouse
description: Set on the River Cam, this warm Cambridge pub is a short walk from the university and a quick hop into the city centre. Expect a buzzing, welcoming atmosphere with a proper pub menu (including Sunday roasts and seasonal specials) plus a wide drinks range of pints, cocktails and soft drinks. There’s a beer garden for relaxed sessions, WiFi and a car park, and it’s set up for families and functions. Sports fans can settle in for live football with Sky Sports and TNT Sports, and there are regular match-day booking options and World Cup/Super Bowl promotions.

name: Corner House
description: A lively Newmarket Road corner pub in Cambridge with Art Deco charm, timber snugs and real ales on tap. Expect a Nepalese-led kitchen alongside pub classics, with hand-pleated momo, slow-braised curries and tandoori grills—plus takeaway and delivery. Matchdays are a big deal: HD screens indoors and an outdoor projector for major fixtures. When the weather’s good, the heated garden and private cabins (with table service) make after-work drinks and easy outdoor dining feel extra special. Great for families and groups, with cosy dining areas and free Wi‑Fi.

name: Lion & Lamb
description: More than three centuries of village history underpin this 17th-century Milton inn, reopened in October 2024 under DSH Hospitality after Stonegate sought new tenants. DSH blends British pub classics with Indian, Nepalese, Japanese and wider Pan-Asian dishes in a long opened-out bar with snug fireplace and heated covered patio. A large garden includes children's play equipment, with dogs and families explicitly welcomed. Up to two well-kept cask ales from national brands sit alongside familiar keg lines, with Monday-to-Friday meal-and-drink deals. Free Wi-Fi and a cosy fireplace make it as much a workspace stop as a weekend lunch destination.

name: The White Horse
description: Milton's White Horse is a roomy village pub on the High Street with a broad beer garden, family-friendly dining and Sky sport for match days. Keg and cask lines include local Milton Brewery beers, and the kitchen turns out grills, burgers and Sunday roasts in a bright, modernised interior. Handy for the science park crowd as well as Milton residents looking for an unpretentious local.

name: The Hole in the Wall
description: Set in Little Wilbraham, this 15th-century Grade II listed pub brings a rustic, country-gastro feel with a snug bar, roaring fires and oak furniture. Expect hand-selected ales, beers and fine wines alongside reinvigorating gastro-quality food, including a traditional Sunday roast (choice of three meats) served 12–4.30pm. With a warm, relaxed atmosphere and table service, it’s a great stop for a proper meal after a day out around Cambridge’s countryside. Pets are welcomed in the snug, bar and outside dining area.

name: The Carlton Arms
description: A traditional community pub just north of Cambridge, run by Trudy Nixon. Expect a relaxed, friendly atmosphere with a strong real-ale reputation, plus draught lagers, cask ales, ciders, wines, spirits and hot drinks. Food is cooked to order using locally sourced, homemade ingredients, with a Sunday carvery served 12–4pm. There’s a big car park and a beer garden with a bouncy castle and children’s play area. Weekly highlights include karaoke every Sunday night and themed food nights (Caribbean Wednesdays, Spanish Fridays). The public bar has a pool table and two dart boards, with teams for both.

name: Waggon & Horses
description: A historic, family-run pub in Milton, reimagined with traditional warmth and contemporary dining. Expect craft ales, cocktails and locally sourced seasonal dishes, plus a family-focused setup with a purpose-built enclosed toddler soft play (0–3s only) and a café area for breakfast and lunch. When the weather’s good, there’s al fresco dining in a spacious, secure garden with an adventure area for little ones. For a longer stay, there are luxury garden pods with private patios, en-suite bathrooms and WiFi—ideal for couples or solo retreats. Entertainment is currently paused, but new things are coming soon.

name: The Ship
description: A newly redeveloped Cambridge pub with a community feel, run by Andy and Mo. Expect a traditional pub menu alongside pizza and curry options, plus a dedicated drinks offering. The standout is the big-screen setup for major matches—listed fixtures for the Euros/World Cup are shown—making it ideal for watching sport with friends. There’s also a games-focused space with pool and darts, giving you plenty to do between rounds. Great for casual meet-ups, match nights, and laid-back evenings with food and drinks.

name: Wilbrahams’ Hall Social Club
description: Nestled inside the Wilbrahams' Memorial Hall complex overlooking the recreation ground, this members' bar serves Great and Little Wilbraham rather than passing trade. The 2016 hall building anchors eighteen community groups and hosts farmers' markets, bridge clubs and village events, with the Social Club opening for coffee mornings, teas and drinks during local functions. Annual membership costs five pounds with forms at the bar. This is a village club rather than a fully fledged public house: CAMRA does not list it among Cambridge pubs, and cask ale is not a focus. Contact the Memorial Hall booking secretary for hall hire enquiries.

name: Sir Isaac Newton
description: Set on Castle Street, this large, airy pub is a comfortable spot for homemade comfort food, from pies to burgers, alongside a wide range of drinks. Regular quiz nights bring a lively, community feel, and it’s very dog friendly—so you can bring your four-legged companion along for a relaxed drink and bite.

name: The Golden Hind
description: A Cambridge Greene King pub with a heritage feel and a big focus on food and drink. Expect ice-cold beers, spirits and pub classics, plus small plates and proper Sunday roasts. There’s a lively beer garden with covered seating, picnic tables, umbrellas and string lights—ideal for post-work catch-ups or weekend sessions. Sports fans can settle in for live football with Sky Sports and TNT Sports, and there’s a dedicated sports booking/fixtures page. Inside you’ll find a games area with a pool table and dartboard, plus WiFi and EV charging. Dogs and families are welcome.

name: The White Horse
description: In the small village of Barton on the A603, this traditional inn is a handy stop near Cambridge and Wimpole Hall. Expect a cosy feel with a classic inglenook fireplace, plus a Thai twist: the kitchen serves an array of Thai cuisine, with the team led by Noi and her experience from the Cambridge area. It’s also a comfortable overnight option with double en-suite rooms, free Wi‑Fi and continental breakfast. A warm, convenient base for visitors heading in and out of Cambridge.

name: The Haymakers
description: A classic High Street pub in Chesterton, Cambridge, serving drinks with a proper kitchen schedule throughout the week. You’ll find weekday hours from lunchtime through late evening, with extended kitchen times on Saturdays and Sundays. It’s set up for walk-ins, with bookings only taken for groups of eight or more to keep space comfortable. Drop in for a relaxed pub stop on the corner of the High Street, and check the kitchen window if you’re planning food.

name: The Brook
description: A family-friendly Indian gastro pub with a traditional dining kitchen and a menu built around Bharat flavours, from butter chicken to naan. The bar focuses on cask ales, craft beers, ciders, cocktails and premium spirits, with low-alcohol and soft drinks plus quality coffee and tea. Set up for match-day energy, it shows TNT Sports on five large screen TVs. There’s a cosy fire for colder days and a garden for summer visits, plus free customer parking in a large car park.

name: Royal Standard
description: A beer-lover’s stop on Mill Road, built around an impressive Belgian draught range, real ale and real cider, plus wines, gins and spirits. The pub is also home to Tzatziki Greek Kitchen, serving souvlakis and other Greek street-food favourites via QR codes for in-house dining and takeaway/delivery. Expect a lively programme of brewery takeovers and collaborations, with CAMRA award recognition for its cider and community credentials. Open daily from midday, with free on-street parking nearby—ideal for a relaxed pint and a proper bite.

name: Kingston Arms
description: Tucked off Mill Road, this cosy side-street free house returned in March 2023 when beer enthusiasts Jethro Scotcher-Littlechild and Mark Donachy rescued it from a brief Mediterranean restaurant spell. CAMRA named it Cambridgeshire Pub of the Year 2025 and the city's first Asset of Community Value. Up to seven cask ales including a dark beer, plus four still ciders, fill pumpclips climbing the ceiling above breweriana and historic festival posters. A heated walled garden stays busy year-round. Trad jazz and occasional gigs complement Tuesday cribbage, monthly quizzes and bi-monthly minibus pub crawls. Snacks, pork pies and pop-up kitchen takeovers supply food.

description: A lively Cambridge pub built around music, craft beer and pizza. Pizza is served daily via Oscar’s Lockdown Pizza, with handmade sourdough bases and a strong vegan selection. The front bar runs monthly tap takeovers (first Thursday) with 10 beers from a single brewer, often paired with street-food vans. Regular nights include quiz (Wednesdays), RPG (Mondays), open-mic scratch (last Thursday), improvised comedy (last Sunday) and a goth club night on the first Friday.

name: The Emperor
description: On the busy corridor between Cambridge station and the historic centre, this single-room pub pairs Latin American tapas with cask and keg beers since a 2015 change of hands. Bare boards, smart unfussy decor and a colourful tiled bar front set the tone, while Latin American artwork lines the walls and an upstairs function room handles larger groups. A decent rear patio garden supports alfresco drinking, and alternate Saturday nights bring Latin dance music. Planning permission granted in 2024 will retain only the Hills Road frontage before offices rise behind, though CAMRA expects trading to continue for now.

name: The Grapes
description: Arbury's capacious community local survives from a 1930s build where white-painted wooden beams and stained-glass windows remain the sole original flourishes. Greene King leases the freehold and pours IPA plus two changing guests from the brewery list. Multiple nooks within the open-plan layout hold pool and darts, a jukebox and Saturday-night live music, while Sky screens show sport. Friday breakfasts run from ten until noon, Sunday roasts draw families, and alternate Tuesday steak nights pull regulars. CAMRA named it City Community Pub 2023. Ample parking, wheelchair access and a beer garden reinforce its role as a welcoming neighbourhood hub on Histon Road.

name: The Anchor
description: A riverside Cambridge favourite set beside the River Cam, with standout views across the water to the Mathematical Bridge and Queens’ College. Settle in for classic ales and seasonal, fresh food, or head to the terrace deck to watch the punts go by. The menu includes a Prix Fixe option (two courses £18, three courses £22, Mon–Thu 12–8pm) plus regular offers like Wing Wednesday and Hello Friday Prosecco bottles. Sports fans can catch matches with Sky Sports and TNT Sports, and there’s a busy events calendar—plus a nod to Pink Floyd on the walls.

name: The Mill
description: Set in a charming 19th-century building on the River Cam, this riverside Cambridge favourite pairs a warm, welcoming feel with a strong real-ale reputation. Expect a seasonal British menu from the head chef, plus bar snacks and a summer Spritz menu. In warmer months you can unwind by the Millpond or in the world’s largest beer garden, while winter brings cosy chats and mulled wine. Big match-day energy is a highlight too, with large screens, great sound and proper atmosphere for the World Cup. Dogs are welcome, and there’s plenty going on with events, parties and private bookings.

name: The Seven Stars
description: A historic Cambridge pub on Newmarket Road, set in a Grade II listed building with a fresh, modern feel after a 2019 renovation. It’s also an Indian restaurant, serving a wide range of drinks alongside a seasonally changing menu of traditional Indian dishes. Expect plenty of vegetarian and vegan options, plus tandoor-cooked kebabs, vegetables and breads, with flavours built around classic spices. With a spacious, welcoming atmosphere and the option to book a table, it’s a great spot for a relaxed dinner just a short cycle from the city centre.

name: The Wrestlers
description: One of the last survivors on a Newmarket Road strip that has lost many locals, this Wells & Co house balances serious Thai cooking with a welcome for drinkers only. The well-lit single bar serves authentic pad thai and regional dishes daily from noon until three and five until nine, drawing office lunch crowds and evening diners who keep the handpumps working alongside Bombardier, Broadside and up to four Brewpoint guest ales. Charles Wells reinvented the interior in the 1990s oriental style and removed the pool table to prioritise tables, a strategy that has kept the Wrestlers consistently busy while neighbours closed.

name: The Pickerel
description: Step into a Cambridge classic with a storied past dating back to 1608, including a former gin palace and old malting-house links. Inside, you’ll find historic brickwork, beams and a fireplace, plus large windows and a comfortable courtyard beer garden for weather-permitting drinks. Expect freshly cooked traditional pub food all week—think hand-battered fish and chips, pie and mash and burgers—with vegan, vegetarian and non-gluten options. The bar is built for catch-ups, with plenty of Greene King favourites and its own beers. Dogs are welcome, and there’s disabled access and facilities. Book ahead for busy moments and special match-day offers.

name: The Granta
description: A historic, waterside pub in Cambridge with a traditional-meets-modern interior and a peaceful beer garden overlooking Mill Pond. Settle in for freshly cooked pub classics all week, plus Sunday roasts and options for vegan, vegetarian and non-gluten choices. There’s plenty to drink, from Greene King favourites to a wide beer range, and you can book for functions, meetings and celebrations. Dog-friendly and family-friendly, with WiFi and takeaway/delivery available. Expect a lively social calendar too—pub quiz nights every Monday and World Cup viewing promotions, with “what’s on” events throughout the year.

name: George Inn
description: Set in the heart of Babraham near Cambridge, this 18th-century coaching inn blends traditional charm with a relaxed, family-run welcome. Expect exposed beams, an open fire and a spacious, well-stocked bar with traditional ales, fine wines and spirits. The kitchen focuses on home-cooked meals with daily specials using fresh, seasonal produce, plus an extensive take-away menu. There’s also a large beer garden and patio, ideal for a slower drink outdoors. The venue is available for weddings, parties and wakes, with a peaceful countryside feel while still being convenient for Cambridge and nearby attractions.

name: The Tram Depot
description: A characterful, historic city-centre bar in Cambridge, set in an iconic building that once served as stables and offices for the horse-drawn tramways. Expect a warm, friendly atmosphere with subtle nods to its past, plus a craft-focused bar offering cask ales, craft beers, ciders, cocktails, wines and spirits. In summer, the sunny terrace is ideal for a relaxed pint. The venue is also a go-to for lively nights out, from music and themed evenings to a monthly folk night and weekly speakeasy jazz jam. Dogs are welcome in the bar.

name: The Eagle
description: Step into a 17th-century, Grade II listed pub in central Cambridge, opposite St Bene’t’s. Expect a warm, historic atmosphere with plenty of reasons to linger: freshly cooked traditional pub food (with vegan, vegetarian and non-gluten options), a wide drinks range and Greene King beers, plus WiFi and delivery. There’s a beer garden for weather-permitting drinks, and the venue is family-friendly and wheelchair accessible. Dogs are welcome too, so everyone can join in. Pop in for coffee, a quick pint after work, or book ahead for occasions like Sunday roast and Christmas.

name: The Bath House
description: In the heart of central Cambridge, this cosy, lively pub is a go-to for drinks, small plates and proper pub classics. Expect a menu worth exploring, plus student discounts and regular “what’s on” moments like quiz nights. Sports fans can settle in for live football across major leagues and competitions, with TNT Sports on hand. It’s also dog-friendly and family-friendly, with WiFi and accessible facilities. Book ahead for events, Sunday roasts, or to secure a seat for big matches and tournament specials.

name: The Lord Byron Inn
operator: Heartwood Collection (reopening as The Meadow Lark)
description: Closed since February 2026 for a major refurbishment, this large 17th-century Trumpington inn on Church Lane is set to reopen late that year as The Meadow Lark under Heartwood Collection, with nineteen bedrooms making it the group's first Cambridgeshire pub with rooms. Before closure, an L-shaped bar with low beams, wood panelling and varied floor levels opened onto a large garden, conservatory function room and purpose-built accommodation wing. Byron's Pool and Trumpington Meadows nature reserve sit nearby. Heartwood promises seasonally changing menus and enhanced outdoor dining inspired by skylarks and the surrounding landscape. Previously traded as the Unicorn.

Chef patron Barry Vera and Star Pubs partners serve contemporary British food from noon, with dogs welcome in bar and garden. Entertainment evenings feature sports personalities and musicians; the terrace seats two hundred. Card payments only.

name: George Inn
description: A friendly neighbourhood spot on Girton’s High Street that shifts from a morning café to a proper pub later on. Start with coffee and pastries, then settle in for traditional pub grub and evening dining, including Tuesday–Saturday dinner service and Sunday summer roast. The vibe is relaxed and welcoming—ideal for students and professionals to work quietly in the daytime, and for locals to chat and mingle as the day winds down. Open late most evenings, with longer weekend hours.

name: Old Crown
description: Set in a historic thatched pub near Cambridge, it’s a cosy spot for Nepalese dining alongside classic pub favourites. There’s a relaxed bar lounge for catching up, plus big-screen live sport for match-day energy. The large free car park and on-site EV chargers make it an easy stop for road trips, family meals and group bookings. When the weather’s good, the garden and terrace are ideal for lingering with craft beer and a pint. Book ahead for major fixtures, or order takeaway for authentic Nepalese dishes and pub classics at home.

name: Portland Arms
description: Basil Oliver's 1930s design overlooks Mitchams Corner's gyratory, sheltering one of Cambridge's most important independent live-music venues inside a lovingly panelled main bar with real fire. A smaller room with pool table opens to a courtyard garden, and the National Inventory recognises the historic interior. Oscar's Pizzas supplies burgers and pub favourites in-house while up to six cask lines mix Greene King guests with Milton and local brews, plus real cider outside winter and extensive bottled craft. Soundproofed back-room gigs accommodate two hundred with in-house PA, making the Portland essential to the city's music scene since decades of band nights.

name: The Bell
description: Bottisham's Bell is a classic chalk-country inn with low beams, open fires and a reputation for well-kept Greene King and guest ales. Lunchtime and evening menus lean on British pub staples, while the garden catches the afternoon sun after walks on the B1102. A settled village local midway between Cambridge and Newmarket that rewards a detour from the A14.

name: Burleigh Arms
description: A historic Cambridge brewery tap with a legacy dating back to the 1820s, now serving modern British plates with seasonal, flavour-led cooking. Food is available on set afternoon and evening windows through the week, with longer hours from Wednesday to Saturday and a shorter Sunday session. Expect a warm, pub atmosphere rooted in local history, plus a kitchen led by Head Chef Sam Sturman. Drop in on Newmarket Road for a proper pint and a well-crafted menu, with booking options available for those planning ahead.

name: St Radegund
description: Tucked at the top of King Street, Cambridge's smallest pub reopened in early 2026 as a cosy, community-driven cask house after years of uncertainty. House beers Sackcloth and Habit Ale build on Milton ales, joined by London Pride and rotating SIBA guests on a handful of handpumps. Memorabilia from the legendary King Street Run and the pub's cricket and rowing clubs lines the walls in a space where every seat feels like the regulars' table.

name: Byron's Bear
description: Set on the River Cam by Jesus Green, this riverside Cambridge pub is all about relaxing with a pint and tucking into proper food. Expect comforting Sunday roasts with seasonal, local produce, plus local ales and a great Guinness. Drop in from morning coffee at the Bear Hatch through to evening drinks, with plenty of space to feast and celebrate. There’s a weekly Sunday quiz, plus special events like World Cup live screenings and themed quiz nights—ideal for groups who want atmosphere and views.

name: The Red Bull
description: A friendly local pub in the heart of Cambridge, with a welcoming bar and a terrace garden for when the weather’s right. Expect a new menu covering light bites through to dinner, plus a solid range of ales and craft beers alongside gins and spirits. It’s a good spot to meet friends for pizza and a drink, with comfortable accommodation available if you want to stay over. Dogs are welcome in the bar and on the terrace, making it easy to bring the whole pack.

name: Red Lion
description: A sixteenth-century village inn on Mill End Road forms the heart of Cherry Hinton social life, recently reopened after refurbishment under Greene King's Hive franchise. Inside, a single room splits into distinct drinking areas around a central fireplace, with an extension hosting occasional live music. A large covered garden draws families and dog walkers, while Sky and TNT screens show Premier League and international fixtures. The Greene King menu runs from weekday lunch deals to Sunday roasts, burgers and pizzas, with pool, darts, quiz nights and karaoke rounding out a classic community local.

name: Fort St George
description: Set by the River Cam, this traditional, heritage-style pub brings old-world charm to riverside Cambridge. It’s a great spot for casual pints, family visits and after-work catch-ups, with function rooms available for celebrations. Dogs are welcome too.

name: Railway Vue
description: Settle into a cosy, community-focused pub atmosphere where darts and pool are part of the fun. Drop in for a relaxed drink with special offers, or catch sports viewing on the day. There’s also a calendar of community events and options for private hire, making it a handy spot for everything from casual catch-ups to group plans. With table bookings available online, it’s easy to plan a visit for afternoons through late evenings.

name: Waggon and Horses
description: Tucked away on a quiet Cottenham back street, this small free house reopened in November 2024 after years closed through the pandemic, following a bright refurbishment under new independent owners. A café-style atmosphere serves cakes and savoury snacks alongside eight keg taps and two rotating real ales from local brewers such as Papworth and Milton. A private rear courtyard offers outdoor seating. Regular events include darts on Monday and Wednesday evenings, board games on Mondays, poker on Wednesdays and a women's darts night on Sundays. CAMRA named it Most Improved Rural Pub 2025.

name: Rose & Crown
description: A relaxed local pub in Histon with afternoon-to-evening opening hours throughout the week. The venue currently has no traditional kitchen, but you can keep an eye on social media for updates and upcoming food trucks. Ideal for a casual pint with friends, with longer hours at weekends for late drinks.

name: The Admiral
description: Standing at the centre of Over village, this Victorian local was formerly the Admiral Vernon before Barry and Jane Arliss and family bought it free of tie and reopened it in July 2024 after a full interior, patio and garden refurbishment. Drinking areas wrap in an L-shape around a wood-panelled bar, with steps up to one room and a larger space leading to a rear patio and beer garden. CAMRA lists freshly produced food with daily specials and Sunday roasts, Adnams Ghost Ship plus Brewpoint seasonal beers and guest ales sold as tasting flights. Three indoor screens show sport, with quiz nights and a Friday meat raffle.

name: Kings Head
description: A friendly neighbourhood pub in Fen Ditton serving wine, beer, spirits and soft drinks. Settle in by the log fire or soak up the Cambridge atmosphere in the sun-drenched beer garden with shady and sunny spots. The venue is gearing up for its opening night on 20 June 2025, and there’s also a private event space in the garden called “The King’s Shed”. Dogs are welcome, with water bowls and treats provided—ideal for a relaxed local catch-up.

name: The Rose
description: A traditional village pub in Stapleford with low ceilings, exposed beams and a cosy bar plus a spacious dining area. Expect a craft ale tap wall, a quieter snug and a family-friendly feel. Food is a highlight: authentic Thai cuisine cooked to order by Thai chefs, plus stone-baked pizzas, fish & chip Fridays and takeaway/click & collect. There’s also a Thursday quiz night for a lively crowd. The snug doubles as a sports spot with a pool table, pro-style darts board and a projector screen for live sport. In warmer weather, there’s an extensive garden and patio.

name: The Sun
description: Overlooking Waterbeach village green, this traditional local lives by a philosophy of good beer and good music. A cosy lounge to the right is dominated by a huge fireplace surrounded by rustic bric-a-brac, while the simply appointed public bar with its woodblock floor stays lively. Seating spreads to the front, a side smoking area and a sun-trap rear garden. An annual beer and music festival runs over the early May bank holiday, with live music at the weekend event and gigs in an upstairs function room. Changing guest ales often include local brews and dark beers. Long-serving licensee Helen stood down in September 2025; the pub reopened after redecoration in October.

name: White Horse
description: Opposite Waterbeach village green, this split-level coaching inn was saved from redevelopment and relaunched in February 2025 by Lapen Inns, the Nepalese hospitality group behind the Old Crown in Girton and Corner House in Cambridge. Wednesday quiz nights, live sports, and dog-friendly spaces including covered terraces make it a renewed community hub on Greenside.

name: George & Dragon
description: A friendly, relaxed gastropub near Cambridge, Huntingdon and St Ives, with a strong focus on fresh fish and seafood plus quality meats. Expect dry-aged steaks, English lamb and British pork and chicken, alongside favourites like lobster, mussels, crabs and seasonal specials. Food is served Wed–Sat with set lunch and evening times, plus Sunday lunch, and there’s also a monthly Tuesday opening for lunch & dinner. Menus include set fish options, Sunday roasts, Friday fish & chips and take-away buffets to go—ideal for an easy night in.

name: Black Horse Inn
description: Set in the heart of Swaffham Bulbeck, this traditional village pub pairs quality drinks with seasonal British food in a relaxed, friendly setting. It’s a good stop for a meal or a pint, with the added bonus of comfortable overnight accommodation. Well-behaved dogs are welcomed, making it easy to bring the whole pack for a cosy visit—whether you’re dropping in for dinner or staying the night.

name: Five Miles Inn
description: Riverside pub and restaurant in Upware, just outside Ely, with views over the River Cam and easy access to Wicken Fen Nature Reserve and Upware Marina. Settle into the light, airy conservatory or the 65-seat restaurant overlooking the water, or keep it casual in the main bar. Expect traditional pub fayre, home-cooked meals, daily-changing specials, and options including gluten-free, vegan and vegetarian. There’s plenty of space indoors plus large gardens with outdoor seating, and ample on-site parking. Dogs are welcome in the garden on leads. Kitchen runs most days until 8pm (earlier on Sundays).

name: Rose and Crown
description: Set in the heart of Ashdon village, this free house pub/restaurant brings classic British hospitality with a distinctive, characterful feel. Expect a strong food focus with a menu covering pub classics, grill dishes and starters, plus standout desserts and plenty of local-produce options. Wines, beers and craft ales are a big part of the offer, with non-alcoholic drinks available too. There’s an easygoing dining-and-drinking vibe, and the terrace is a highlight when the sun’s out—ideal for lunch, dinner and weekend roasts. Table bookings are available.

name: Earl of Derby
description: A friendly Cambridge pub with bed-and-breakfast comfort, offering a choice of full or continental breakfast and en-suite rooms designed for a relaxed stay. With twelve large en-suite rooms (plus shower rooms), free Wi‑Fi and tea/coffee facilities, it’s a convenient base near the rail station and within an easy walk of the city centre. Guests also mention home-cooked pub food for breakfast and dinner, plus welcoming staff and entertaining evening events. Ideal if you want a local-feel pub atmosphere with overnight accommodation and a straightforward, comfortable routine.

name: The Bell Inn
description: A popular community two-bar pub on West Wickham Road, purchased in spring 2018 by a local resident after years as a Greene King house and now run independently. The public bar offers a jukebox, pub games and television, while the wood-panelled lounge suits diners and drinkers alike with tasty homemade food at affordable prices, Sunday roasts and occasional food vans on Mondays. Changing ales always include a mild or dark beer, with locally produced ciders often available. A large rear beer garden features cosy sheds for wet weather, and a quiz runs on the last Tuesday of each month. New licensees took over in September 2025.

name: White Horse
description: A pleasant two-bar village local on Longstanton Road where the left-hand room functions as a restaurant serving popular British cuisine and the right-hand drinking bar retains bare-board floors, plain bench seating, an open fire and framed photos of old Oakington. Patio doors lead to an attractive large garden with front tables too. Regular events include darts on winter Mondays, poker on Tuesdays, pétanque on summer Wednesdays and quiz night on Thursdays. Greene King IPA is a regular beer with changing guests. A two-bedroom cottage is available for holiday lets. Registered Asset of Community Value and a popular village meeting place.

name: Hat & Rabbit
description: A family-friendly village pub in Fulbourn, just a short hop from Cambridge, with a welcoming bar serving cask and craft beers and ciders. Expect traditional, home-cooked pub dining made fresh to order, including starters, mains, vegetarian/vegan and gluten-free options, plus a much-loved Sunday roast. There’s also a coffee shop inside the pub with cakes and pastries, and breakfast on Friday and Saturday. Outside, a newly refurbished beer garden includes a garden kitchen and bar (The Hutch) for pizzas, burgers, hotdogs and chips. Quiz night runs monthly, and a large conservatory dining room is available for private events.

name: Black Horse
description: A relaxed East Anglia cider pub with a friendly, community feel. Expect real ales, independent beers and local ciders, plus a rotating cask line-up and plenty of alcohol-free options. Food is available most days with homemade cakes and chips on Wednesdays and Sundays, and a full menu on other evenings (with a food van on the last Sunday of the month). Dogs are welcome throughout on leads, and families are encouraged in a calm, adult-focused atmosphere. There’s a quiz every Thursday, plus regular open mic/jam sessions and other seasonal events. Board games, drawing materials and WiFi help keep younger visitors entertained.

name: Six Bells
description: Set in Covent Garden, Cambridge, this traditional local pub sits just off Mill Road and feels deceptively spacious. Expect two bars plus a conservatory with comfy sofas, a pool room, patio garden, dartboard and a jukebox for laid-back evenings. The drink list leans classic: five real ales, rotating guest ales, lagers (including Carlsberg and San Miguel), Aspells cider, and Guinness, alongside wines, spirits and minerals. With free wireless broadband available and a steady calendar of events, it’s a friendly stop for a chill pint and good company.

name: The Crown
description: A charming beamed country pub in a quiet village setting, about 2 miles from Saffron Walden and a short walk from Home Farm Fishery. Expect a proper pub drinks list with real ales on cask, plus lagers, Guinness, cider, wines and traditional spirits. Food is freshly prepared to order, with homecooked favourites like steak & mushroom pie, lasagne, burgers and fish & chips, alongside vegetarian options, sandwiches and baguettes. Sunday dining brings classic roasts. There are also en-suite rooms for stays, with breakfast options—ideal for a countryside day out and an easy return.

name: John Barleycorn Pub
description: Built in 1660 as a coaching house, this thatched-roof inn on Moorfield Road in Duxford retains many original features within a single food-led bar where tables serve diners yet a distinct area welcomes drinkers only. Up to four real ales and Weston's Old Rosie cider are available, with a car park and garden to the rear and front drinking tables. En-suite accommodation in a block at the rear is scheduled to restart in March 2026 alongside a new children's play area. The pub closed in July 2025 and reopened under new Red Comb Pubs management on 4 December 2025, two miles from Imperial War Museum Duxford.

name: White Horse Inn
description: Occupying a fine old building in Swavesey's former market area, this historic seventeenth-century inn was long regarded as one of Cambridgeshire's finest community pubs. The classic public bar features polished floor tiles, beamed ceiling, wood panelling and an elevated fireplace, with later additions including a lounge dining area, pool and function rooms, and a large garden with play equipment. Locally sourced home-cooked food ranged from sandwiches and pizzas to hearty mains and Sunday lunch. CAMRA Community Rural Pub of the Year 2020. The pub closed on 25 March 2026 when the Bonson family ceased trading; a local campaign seeks to save and reopen it.

name: Golden Ball Inn
description: A sixteenth-century thatched country inn on Boxworth High Street, transformed by a major renovation that replaced a flat bar roof with a pitched vault draped in Latin-script tapestries, added a conservatory leading to patio and an impressive garden, and attached a ten-room detached hotel annex. Heavily food-led with a strong reputation, the venue also maintained a large bar area serving Brewpoint regulars. Wells and Co operated the pub until it closed at the end of June 2025. CAMRA reported in March 2026 that work is underway with the aim of reopening in May 2026 under new management, though it remains closed at time of research.

name: Hare & Hounds
description: A community-owned free house in Harlton with a classic pub feel and a busy, welcoming weekly rhythm. Open daily from midday to late, it’s known for its cider credentials (Cambridge Cider Pub of the Year in 2022 and 2023). Food is a big part of the plan: the kitchen is reopening after renovations, with a limited menu at first, plus a Sunday BBQ and sides. Expect Friday fish and chips evenings and a Sunday 8pm pub quiz—booking is advised if you want to eat inside at peak times.

name: The Black Bull
description: A family-run local in Longstanton known for Chinese comfort food, with pizzas, burgers and wraps served in the restaurant, as bar snacks or for takeaway. Drop in for a drink and a bite, then settle into the bar area with a pool table. The pub also puts on regular live-music nights, including a rock party with free entry. When the weather’s good, enjoy your pint in the beer garden. With space for birthday parties, anniversaries and other celebrations, it’s a friendly spot for both daytime and evening get-togethers.

name: White Horse
description: A straightforward village local on Foxton High Street with a U-shaped layout where one slightly raised arm serves as a games area with a pool table. A pétanque court sits in the garden behind this friendly warm pub, which changed hands in January 2020 and serves three changing cask ales. Food is available regularly including Friday fish and chips and Sunday lunch, with terrestrial TV and football coverage. Reviews praise a clean atmosphere, welcoming staff and reasonably priced roasts. Foxton railway station is roughly six hundred metres away, making it accessible for walkers exploring the Cam valley villages south of Cambridge.

name: The Bank Micropub
description: Opened in late 2012 within a former village bank on Willingham High Street, this single-room micropub centres on a short bar rescued from a closed Cambridge pub, with walls decorated in photos of local interest. Beers pour direct from cask, KeyKeg or keg, alongside a well-stocked fridge of cans and bottles and a range of still, kegged and bottled ciders. There is no kitchen, but changing food vans park nearby on Saturday evenings from 5–8pm. Closed Sunday and Monday, the Bank offers a warm welcome where casual visitors are quickly drawn into local conversation—a social hub that arguably serves the village better than banking ever did.

name: The Plough
description: A recently renovated L-shaped village local on Great Shelford's High Street pairs sage-green panelling and cream walls with assorted furniture and framed village photographs. Hawthorn Leisure's free house pours Greene King IPA plus two rotating guest ales from the SIBA list, while a large family-friendly garden and pool table draw weekend crowds. Big-screen sport covers major fixtures, live music appears at least monthly, and pizzas and burgers supplement the bar offer. Dog-friendly and close to Shelford station, it sits a few miles south of Cambridge city centre.

name: White Lion
description: Reopened in November 2022 after refurbishment, this Grade II listed former coaching inn opens from a grey-beamed main bar with three handpumps and BrewBoard keg lines. Pieminister pies and mash are served from the bar, with food vans Wednesday through Sunday, while a separate billiards room hosts meetings and functions. Behind the pub, a car park, pétanque court, covered beer garden and smoking area complete a compact village high-street destination independent of any national chain.

name: The Greyhound
description: The largest of Sawston's Grade II listed High Street pubs wears its timber and exposed wood handsomely in a busy dining-led room that still keeps real ale on Adnams Broadside, Greene King IPA and Sharp's Doom Bar. Lunchtime, evening and Sunday menus drive trade, with Venture Pub Company ownership following a 2018 refurb after earlier tenant changes. A beer garden, parking and disabled access support family visits, and a new manager arrived in December 2024. Ale may not be the headline, but the beers are consistently well kept.

name: Tickell Arms
description: Set in the heart of Whittlesford, this country pub and restaurant is a short hop from Duxford and the M11. Expect seasonal modern British cooking, Sunday roasts, and a relaxed dining vibe with real fires in winter. Outside, there’s a conservatory/terrace overlooking a pond and rose garden, plus two gardens including a beer garden for light bites and a wide range of drinks. The pub bar serves up to four local real ales and an extensive wine list by the glass. Dogs are welcome in the pub area, where you can also eat if tables are available.

name: Duke of Wellington
description: Exposed beams, three open fires and scrubbed candlelit tables lend rustic warmth to this low-ceilinged Willingham village local, sold by Greene King and reopened free of tie in April 2025 after refurbishment. Bare-boarded floors and a rear car park opening onto a garden create an unpretentious drinking space pouring up to four cask ales from local breweries. Food is not currently offered, but dog-friendly garden seating, quiz nights and occasional live music keep the community returning after a brief autumn 2025 closure.

name: Dyke's End
description: Set in the peaceful village of Reach at the edge of the Devil’s Dyke, this free house is a cosy countryside stop for walkers and locals alike. Expect a well-stocked bar with cask ales, lagers, wines, British gin and soft drinks. Inside there’s a refurbished cosy bar, a larger dining area with a log burner, plus an upstairs dining room. Step outside to a front garden overlooking the Village Green (home to the Reach Fair) and a rear garden tucked among fruit trees—ideal for relaxed drinks in the open air. Family and dog friendly.

name: Crown & Thistle
description: Built in 1528 as the Chequers and extended in 1603 into a coaching inn, this freehouse guards one of Essex's earliest inglenook fireplaces and a legend that James I stopped here en route to his coronation. Today an independent operation pairs a relaxed bar with a restaurant serving authentic Thai cuisine and stone-baked pizzas, backed by real ales, wines and gins. Patio seating and a heated smoking area sit outside, dogs are welcome, and locals and the village cricket team remain loyal regulars.

name: The Plough
description: A traditional village pub with a long history, serving real ales, ciders, lagers, wines and spirits. Expect good homemade pub food six days a week, plus roast dinners on Sundays, with takeaway available Monday–Friday evenings. The team welcomes you with a friendly, community feel, and there’s plenty to keep you entertained: darts, crib, cards, pool and dominos. With sports branding shown for TNT Sports and Sky Sports, it’s a great spot to drop in for a drink and settle in for the game.

name: The Old Red Lion
description: Set in the countryside village of Horseheath near Cambridge, this traditional pub and restaurant is a calm, welcoming stop for locals and visitors. Expect seasonal menus with locally sourced ingredients, plus a popular Sunday roast and festive Christmas dining. After dinner, stay in one of 12 spacious ensuite rooms for a proper break. The vibe is cosy and friendly, with guests praising the food, service and comfortable rooms—ideal for a leisurely meal or a quiet overnight stay with your dog.

name: White Swan
description: A family-run village pub in Stow-Cum Quy, Cambridge, set in a timber-framed building dating back to the 17th century. Expect a welcoming local-and-visitor atmosphere with real ales and pub food at the heart of the menu. Booking is advisable, and opening hours vary through the week, with Mondays and Tuesdays closed and midweek/ weekend sessions running into the evening.

name: The Hop Bind
description: Set in the heart of Cottenham, this old coaching inn brings a classic, comfortable pub feel with a cosy log burner and a warm welcome. Expect a wide range of beers, lagers, ciders and nearly 30 gins, plus pub snacks. Sports fans can settle in with the latest sporting events on multiple screens, with BT and Sky Sports and extra matches on terrestrial TV when there’s demand. There’s also pool and darts, and a heated beer garden for relaxed drinks in the open air.

name: Square and Compasses
description: A traditional pub in Great Shelford built around straightforward, easy-to-choose food. Expect burgers and allergen-friendly Sunday lunch, plus a well-kept beer selection. Drop in for a relaxed drink, dine with friends, or settle in by the fireplace—there’s also the option to eat al fresco. The menu is designed to be clear and accommodating for dietary needs, making it a comfortable spot for casual meals and longer visits alike.

name: The Regal
description: Art-deco bones from Cambridge's 1937 Regal cinema frame one of the city's largest Wetherspoon halls, spread across two floors with a licensed rear patio when it opened in 2000. Four regular cask ales and eight to ten guests rotate through busy handpump banks, complemented by Weston's and Gwynt y Ddraig ciders and streamlined value food from morning to late night. Sport screens, board games and a Friday-Saturday DJ from ten o'clock animate the barn-like space, though weekend queues can test patience in this central landmark.

name: Royal Oak
description: Step into a 14th-century village pub on Barrington’s long village green, set in the countryside with a warm, local feel. The bar serves sharing snacks, while the restaurant turns out classic and modern pub dishes with sustainable seafood, plus standout Sunday roasts. On select dates there are themed evenings like a Greek Night. Dogs are welcome in the pub area and you can also dine outside on the green or beneath the oak and walnut trees. There’s also an outdoor bar and pizzeria called The Old Tuck Shop (seasonal), overlooking the green.

name: Kings Head
description: Set in the heart of Sawston, this traditional British pub pairs a premium-value bar with a large sunny beer garden and a cosy bar and snug warmed by a wood-burning stove in winter. Expect quality ales, guest cask, premium lagers, Guinness, cider, plus cocktails on tap and a solid gin and wine selection. There’s also a strong guest-stay offering: refurbished en-suite rooms near Cambridge, including a family option, doubles, and a self-contained cottage with free parking and Wi‑Fi. TNT Sports is shown in the bar, and the venue runs community charity events and a pub quiz.
